thread:
Olivia: Heads-up — we got a spike on the Billing dashboard this morning showing embeddings usage up 6x for a handful of big tenants. looks like it started around the v3 clientlib rollout window.
Sam: I saw that too. embeddings count -> unit price jump, but raw token volumes didn't match. suspicious mapping change?
Ravi: Quick theory: v3 sends a new header `X-embed-mode: true` and also includes `billing_context.type`. the transform service currently only checks `content_type` and falls back to text if billing_context is missing. if v3 omitted content_type in some paths we might have misclassified as text vs embedding (or vice versa).
Marta: Confirmed in logs. sample from tenant123: payload has billing_context={"kind":"embedding","dims":1536} but content_type was null. transformer emitted event with unit_type="text_tokens". meter aggregator applies text pricing and embedding pricing differently, causing double-reporting in downstream rollups.
Olivia: Oof. So pipeline path: edge -> enrich (adds billing_context) -> transform (classifies unit_type) -> aggregator -> billing ledger. transform got updated last release to prefer `content_type` over billing_context, so if content_type is absent -> default to text. v3 sometimes sends only billing_context.
Sam: Do we have a short-term mitigation? we can patch transform to prefer billing_context if present, or add a mapping rule: if billing_context.kind == embedding then set unit_type=embedding.
Ravi: I pushed a quick branch with the mapping. small change: in transform service mapping function:```python
# map event -> unit_type
if event.get('billing_context', {}).get('kind') == 'embedding':
    unit = 'embedding'
elif event.get('content_type') == 'text':
    unit = 'text'
else:
    unit = 'text'
```
Marta: Nice. Any risk to invoices if we flip behavior mid-day?
Olivia: We'll only enable feature flagged on a canary topic (tenant sampling 5%) and monitor ledger deltas. if stable for 30m, roll to 25% then 100%. alerting on delta >2% per-tenant.
deploy-bot: Deploy queued: transform/mapping-fix -> canary (5%) at commit 2a7f9c. scheduled in 2m.
Sam: Also create a dashboard panel that compares embedding_unit_count vs embedding_charge_count (post- vs pre- transform) to catch mismatch early. I can add a derived metric in Grafana using the new event tag.
Marta: We need a reconciliation query for finance to audit affected tenants. Draft SQL:```sql
SELECT tenant_id,
  SUM(CASE WHEN unit_type='embedding' THEN units ELSE 0 END) AS embedding_units,
  SUM(CASE WHEN reported_price_bucket='embedding' THEN charge_units ELSE 0 END) AS embedding_charges,
  COUNT(*) AS events
FROM billing_events
WHERE ts >= now() - interval '48 hours'
GROUP BY tenant_id
ORDER BY embedding_units DESC
LIMIT 50;
```
Ravi: I'll instrument a short-lived metric in transform: `transform.classify.overrides` tagged with previous_class and new_class so we can see how many events would flip.
Olivia: Good. Ops playbook: if canary shows invoice divergence >1% for any tenant with >$500/day spend, rollback immediately. If smaller tenants show divergence but stable, continue with staged rollout.
Sam: Also add a migration shim: backfill-transform job that reprocesses the last 24h raw events to regenerate canonical unit_type and write to staging ledger for finance to compare. This can be heavy; only run for a whitelist of tenants for now.
Marta: I'll coordinate whitelist with account-ops. can we tag those reprocessed events to avoid double-billing? mark them as `reprocess=true` and don't include in live totals until finance sign-off.
Ravi: Canary deployed. Initial metric: transform.classify.overrides = 0.02% of canary events (expected). embedding_units in canary tenants align with raw dims.
Olivia: Great. keep the canary running 30m, then expand to 25%. if deploy-bot reports any downstream aggregator lag, pause.
deploy-bot: Canary started: transform/mapping-fix @ canary-topic (5%).
metering-bot: Alert (medium): embedding_charge_count increased by +12% in dashboard 'billing:unit_mix' at 03:12 UTC
Sam: seeing the alert, but that's aggregated across all tenants. canary tenants look fine. likely old misclassified events still in pipeline.
Marta: I opened a ticket with finance (FIN-487) and uploaded the reconciliation SQL results snapshot to the ticket.
Olivia: Next steps: 1) let canary run 30m, 2) run backfill for 10 high-spend tenants with reprocess tag, 3) prepare an incident note if we need to adjust invoices/credits. Who can take the backfill?
Ravi: I can run backfill for the whitelist tonight - ETA 2 hours (staged job).
Sam: I'll update the Grafana to include a per-tenant delta card and wire an alert for >2% divergence.
Marta: I'll notify CS for potential customer outreach in case we need to issue temporary credits.
Olivia: Thanks all. keep pings in this thread. I'll own the postmortem and patch notes for the billing contract change so devs don't repeat this. :thumbsup:
